whatever had been asked for. A blueprint of the wrong kingdom is worse than no blueprint.

detail.the_bug_this_replaces: Until this run, that description produced a blueprint of Metazoa -- ALL ANIMALS -- with 8 organ systems, 38 organs and 138 cell types. The taxon silently defaulted to the widest animal clade whenever no taxon word was recognised, on the reasoning that the widest taxon removes no structure by taxon constraint. The reasoning is sound and the behaviour was not: the fallback does not merely relax the constraints, it decides what the organism IS. The word "bacterium" sat in words_not_recognised while the tool built an animal with organs, and nothing connected the two.

body: "eats carbon" has at least four readings and they are different organisms: fixing CO2 from the air (autotrophy, which cyanobacteria and plants already do everywhere), oxidising hydrocarbons (Alcanivorax and the oil-degrading guild), depolymerising plastic (Ideonella sakaiensis on PET), or consuming elemental carbon, which essentially nothing does. This run takes the first reading and says so. No layer here disambiguates a request; the words are not read as English, and a tool that silently picked one of four would be guessing in the same way the Metazoa default was.

detail.why: it is the reading with a real industrial chassis to name: Cupriavidus necator fixes CO2 through the Calvin cycle using hydrogen as the electron donor.

body: the scientific name resolves (Cupriavidus necator, NCBITaxon_106590) and the hierarchy that comes back is almost empty: 2 organ system(s), 6 organ(s), 1 tissue(s), 1 cell type(s). That is not a failure of the query. Uberon is an ANIMAL anatomy ontology and the Cell Ontology is overwhelmingly animal cell types, so for a prokaryote there is almost nothing in them to find. The anatomical layer of this system has close to nothing to say about most of life, and saying that plainly is better than a thin hierarchy that looks like a result.

body: a STATE resolves for a bacterium. Two fields have values because the design declared them, every other field is null with its reason, and each declared value carries kind "assumed" and the source the designer gave -- so nothing downstream can mistake a stated picogram for a weighed one. Before this a taxon base resolved no STATE at all and organism_get refused outright, which meant no scenario, no standing check and no physics could be asked about any organism outside the bundle.

detail.caveat: This document names a TAXON and carries a DECLARED parameter set: quantities the designer stated, each with a source saying where it came from. Nobody measured them on this organism, and the engine holds measured parameters only for the organisms in its bundle. Every declared value enters STATE with kind "assumed", so the weakest-input machinery and every model_confidence downstream carry the fact that a person stated it. A result computed from them is a statement about those declarations as much as about the organism; fields nobody declared stay null and the checks that need them still refuse.

body: The design says "swims". A blueprint cannot answer that: a part list describes one instant and swimming is a cycle. Ask the locomotion layer for the obvious first design -- a paddle that opens and closes, the way anything our size would swim.

why: does a paddle move a bacterium?

body: IMPOSSIBLE, by a theorem and not by a simulation: the stroke is time-reversible (declared reciprocal) and Re <= 9.96e-5 everywhere in the stated ranges. In the Stokes limit the displacement over a cycle depends on the PATH through configuration space and not on the rate, so a path that retraces itself returns the body exactly where it started. Net displacement per cycle is zero, at any beat frequency. This is the strongest verdict anything in this repository can return short of Lean: not "unlikely", not "inefficient", but zero net displacement per cycle, at any beat frequency, for any organism whose stroke retraces its own path at this Reynolds number. Driving the power stroke faster than the recovery stroke -- the obvious fix, and the one intuition suggests -- changes nothing, because in the Stokes limit the displacement depends on the PATH through configuration space and not on the rate.

detail.theorem: Purcell EM 1977, Life at low Reynolds number, Am J Phys 45(1):3-11
detail.limiting_factor: the stroke is time-reversible (declared reciprocal) and Re <= 9.96e-5 everywhere in the stated ranges. In the Stokes limit the displacement over a cycle depends on the PATH through configuration space and not on the rate, so a path that retraces itself returns the body exactly where it started. Net displacement per cycle is zero, at any beat frequency.
detail.what_would_fix_it: break the time-reversal symmetry: a rotating helix, a travelling wave along a flagellum, or a cilium whose recovery stroke follows a different path from its power stroke. Two or more degrees of freedom moved out of phase trace a loop, and a loop encloses area, and enclosed area is displacement.

body: The theorem names its own escape: break the time-reversal symmetry. A rotating helix traces a loop in configuration space rather than retracing a line, and a loop encloses area, and enclosed area is displacement. That is what a flagellum is. Declare the cycle too, so the arithmetic can be checked against the speed asked for.

body: Every layer so far asked whether the design is internally possible. None of them asked the question that decides whether most organisms exist: is there anywhere it could live that is not already full of something better at living there? Carbon fixation is the most thoroughly occupied trade on the planet.

why: where is this clade recorded, what else is there, and what is recorded as interacting with it

body: GBIF holds 89 occurrence records for Cupriavidus necator A, concentrated in CN, IN, US. In the Rhine-Main agricultural belt, Germany GBIF holds 18 records; the 10 most-recorded non-Aves species are listed. No population parameters were declared, so whether this design could establish against what is there has NOT been evaluated. That question needs numbers no occurrence database contains.

recorded_range.reading: GBIF holds 89 occurrence records for Cupriavidus necator A, concentrated in CN, IN, US.
recorded_range.caveat: Occurrence records are presence and collector effort. They are heavily biased toward wealthy countries, roadsides, protected areas and charismatic taxa. A blank map is a map of where nobody looked as often as it is a map of where the organism is not.

Acinetobacter guillouiae Nemec et al., 2010 (1 records)

detail.relationships_note: Grouped from GloBI's own interaction types. 0 taxa recorded eating this clade, 0 recorded parasitising it, 0 in a recorded mutualistic or symbiotic relationship with it, 0 it is recorded hosting. COMPETITION IS NOT AMONG THEM, and that is not an oversight: competition is the one ecological relationship that leaves almost no direct observational trace, because it is two organisms NOT doing something to each other. GloBI records interactions that somebody watched happen. Nobody watches an exclusion. Types this grouping does not recognise, left in "other": hasVector.
cannot_say: whether the design would be outcompeted: that needs growth rates, carrying capacities and competition coefficients, and none of them is in an occurrence record or an interaction record
how abundant anything is: occurrence counts are records, which is sampling effort as much as biology
whether the design could eat what is there, or be eaten by what is there: the interaction records are for its CLADE, and a design is by construction not its clade
anything about the places nobody has surveyed, which is most places
anything about Aves, which is filtered out of every result here by design and is a central part of most terrestrial communities

body: The databases hold no population parameter, so the tool will not say whether the design is outcompeted -- it will only say so from numbers somebody declares. Declare them, as the designer's own estimates, and let the criterion run. The answer is then a property of those four numbers and the run says so.

why: the mutual invasibility criterion, from declared parameters

body: Against resident soil autotroph guild, the design CANNOT invade when rare: at the resident's carrying capacity its per-capita growth rate is negative. It is excluded, on these parameters.

invader K.source: DESIGN INPUT: cells per gram of soil the designed strain is assumed to reach alone. An estimate by the designer, not a measurement; soil carrying capacities for a specific strain are not in GBIF or GloBI and were not looked up.

resident K.source: DESIGN INPUT: the standing community assumed an order of magnitude denser, on the reasoning that it is already there and adapted. An estimate, not a measurement.

alpha, resident on invader.source: DESIGN INPUT: residents assumed to suppress the invader almost as strongly as the invader suppresses itself, because they compete for the same inorganic carbon and the same electron donors.

alpha, invader on resident.source: DESIGN INPUT: the invader assumed to suppress residents weakly, being rare and novel.

detail.model_caveat: Lotka-Volterra two-species competition: phenomenological, no space, no age structure, no environmental variation, no evolution, no third species, and one competition coefficient standing for every way two organisms can get in each other's way. The outcome above is a property of the four numbers that were declared. It is as good as they are and no better, and every one of them is an input to this result rather than an output of it.

asked: could this organism establish anywhere, against what is already there
what_it_taught: On the designer's own four numbers the strain cannot invade when rare: at the resident guild's carrying capacity its per-capita growth rate is negative, so it is excluded. That outcome is a property of those four numbers and not a measurement of anything, and the run says so twice. What the real databases contribute is the other half: where the clade is actually recorded, what is actually in the chosen box, and what is actually recorded as interacting with it -- facts with studies behind them, and no population parameter anywhere among them.

performance_criteria.source_text: Cupriavidus necator that eats carbon dioxide

why: the first set of numbers the designer proposed

body: Carbon leaving exceeds carbon entering at every corner of the stated ranges: 1.20e-14-1.20e-14 mol C/day out against 1e-14 mol C/day in. That is not an optimistic design, it is an impossible one -- the shortfall has to come from somewhere, and there is nowhere.

detail.model: Conservation of mass on the carbon: uptake >= biomass + respired.
detail.model_caveat: A steady-state balance over one day on ONE element. It says nothing about the energy budget, which is where carbon fixation is actually expensive -- the Calvin cycle costs ATP and reducing equivalents, and an organism can be in carbon balance and nowhere near energy balance. It says nothing about nitrogen, phosphorus or any other limiting element, nothing about whether the uptake rate is achievable by any transporter, and nothing about rate: a balance that holds per day may be unreachable per second.

why: the same design with a claim that does not break conservation of mass

body: The carbon adds up at every corner: 1e-14 mol C/day in against 9.50e-15-9.50e-15 mol C/day out, a biomass yield of 0.55-0.55 mol C per mol C taken up. The correction is the loop doing its job: the first set of numbers was not pessimistic or optimistic, it was impossible, and the check said which atoms were missing rather than scoring the design badly.

cannot_say: whether the organism can achieve the declared uptake rate: no transporter kinetics, no surface-area limit, no diffusion model
whether the energy to fix that carbon is available

genotype.note: unchanged: nothing here connects a gene to a flux, which is the mechanism gap the mass-balance check states rather than hides.

what_it_taught: The request is answerable at last. The first numbers the designer proposed claimed more carbon leaving as biomass and CO2 than entered, which conservation of mass forbids outright -- and the check said impossible rather than unlikely. Corrected, the balance holds at a 55 percent yield. What the check still cannot say is everything about whether the organism could do it: no transporter kinetics, no energy budget, and carbon fixation is expensive in ATP rather than in carbon.
